angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 380,548 km at 30.89 pc = 0.16 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 32.3697 +/- 0.0241 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 30.89 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.547 +/- 0.025 solar radii from Mallorquín et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1801 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...680A..76M/abstract): 380,548 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.556 +/- 0.042 solar masses from Mallorquín et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1801 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...680A..76M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3863 +/- 77 K from Mallorquín et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1801 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...680A..76M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mallorquín et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1801 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...680A..76M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1801.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.707, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
